public_rationale: The claim is absolute: LLMs had taught us nothing at all about why the world or the human mind is as it is. Before the post, a peer-reviewed PNAS paper (2021) said transformer language models gave explicit evidence that predictive processing shapes human language comprehension. On an ordinary reading, that is at least some insight into the mind. But the speaker's bar is explanation of why things are this way 'rather than some other way', which is Chomsky's standard. Critics, Marcus among them, would say model-to-brain fits are prediction or correlation, not explanation. The result depends on that contested standard, which the speaker did not define. Nothing I found settles it either way.
limitations: Rests on one counterexample. I did not survey the wider literature.
The explanatory standard is philosophical, and reasonable experts disagree on it.
